title: Sacrifices Fest
reviewNotes: Three branches from seven pieces after Kxg3 at 148s. Source final queen offers Qg1/Kf3/Qf1/Ke3/Qc1 force Rxc1 Kxb2, then Rc2+ Kb1 Rc4; b8=Q is explicitly completed independently. Immediate Rxg1 comparison wins. A different king retreat Kf4 makes immediate Qf1+ a drawing mistake, with Ke5 the checked drawing reply; Ke3 and rook capture do not preserve that draw. Earlier ten/eight-piece play remains context.

But black is not that naive and in this position he doesn't take the queen and instead plays the very precise rook to B2 check. This prepares to collect the white pawn before it promotes. If now the king tries to go back to repeat moves, he's actually going to allow us to fork the king and rook and successfully pick up the two rooks. But black is smart. He's not going to do that. Instead, he just collects the white pawn. But unfortunately, removing that pawn does not help black. And now the walk of shame starts. Queen to G1 check. King to F3. Queen to F1 check. King to E3.
